subject: Audit log handback: format options, TTL matrix, and deletion flow
messages:
From: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@medicorps.com>
To: avery_johnson@redwood.ai
Cc: compliance@medicorps.com
Date: 2027-09-01T08:34:00Z
Subject: Request: Audit log export formats + deletion evidence

Hi Avery,

Thanks for taking this — our compliance team needs a short write-up describing the ways Redwood can hand back tenant audit/access logs for legal review. Specifically:
- Supported export formats (NDJSON, CSV, Parquet?) and per-message metadata preserved (timestamp, user-id, tenant-id, request-id, ip).
- A sample manifest for large exports and how we reference chunking/offsets.
- Proof of deletion timeline/erase confirmation once we request purge.
- Any SLA you offer for bulk handbacks (typical size: ~8TB compressed over ~90 days) and secure transfer options (SFTP, AWS snowball, signed URL).

Can you send a concise matrix we can attach to our evidence pack by EOD Wed? If you prefer a quick call, Sara & I are available tomorrow morning.

Thanks,
Sara
Director of Compliance
Medicorps Health

[Attachment: request_summary.pdf]
From: avery_johnson@redwood.ai
To: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@medicorps.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-09-01T11:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: Audit log export formats + deletion evidence

Sara — thanks for the clear list. Putting Marissa and Karthik on this for export/playbook details. High level answers here, we'll follow up with a concise matrix and sample manifest attached: 

1) Formats: Primary delivery is newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON) for event streams; we can also provide CSV for delimited fields and Parquet on request for analytics-friendly delivery. NDJSON preserves event-level metadata (ts, user_id, tenant_id, request_id, ip, service, operation).

2) Manifest & chunking: Exports are chunked by time window and size (default 10GB compressed per file). Each manifest lists chunk filename, byte-range, start/end timestamps, record count, and a SHA256 hash. We include a top-level index file for large exports.

3) Deletion proof: After a handback-plus-deletion request, we provide an erase report with: export manifest id, deletion request timestamp, list of affected storage objects, and a signed deletion token. For longer retention (legal hold) we can freeze deletion and provide a hold identifier.

4) Transfer options and SLA: Secure HTTPS signed URL (short-lived), SFTP over dedicated transfer endpoint, or direct cloud-to-cloud (S3 cross-account). For very large sets we support physical transfer (partner snowball-like). Typical turnaround SLA for full-tenant handback: 10 business days for <2TB, 20 business days for 2–10TB, negotiable for >10TB.

We'll attach a one-page TTL/format matrix and a sample manifest. If anything else needed, call out the fields you care most about.

—Avery
Head of Customer Ops, Redwood Inference
[Redwood logo]
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Sara Lopez <sara.lopez@medicorps.com>, avery_johnson@redwood.ai
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-09-02T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: Audit log export formats + deletion evidence

Hi Sara — attaching the TTL/format matrix and a sample manifest as promised. A few notes inline: 

- Field preservation: we always include original event payload plus a normalized header. If you want additional headers (e.g., geolocation resolved), we can add that as a post-processing step (extra cost).
- Hashing: each chunk is hashed; we also provide a manifest-level Merkle-ish verification chain so you can validate completeness.
- Time windows: Exports are based on customer UTC windows; if you need preservation by local timezone we can map on the manifest.

Attachment list: audit_export_sample_20270901.ndjson (sample chunk), redwood-export-manifest.csv (index), sla-retention-matrix.pdf (TTL table).

Marissa
Product Ops, Redwood Inference

- For S3 cross-account transfer: do you support bucket-level replication with object-lock retention mode preserved during handback?
- Can you provide a template deletion attestation we can keep in our records?

We'd like to schedule a 30-minute call to walk through the manifest and hash verification next week. Availability: Tue 9/7 0900–1100 PT or Wed 9/8 1300–1500 PT.

Sara

Date: 2027-09-03T16:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: Audit log export formats + deletion evidence

Sara — quick answers to the compliance bullets: 

1) Retention metadata emitted: created_at (event), ingested_at, last_accessed_at (if requested), retention_status (active/held/expired), tombstone_ts (when object flagged for deletion). We include per-record retention_status in the manifest when an erase is requested.

2) S3 cross-account: We do not preserve customer-side object-lock during a cross-account copy. Our recommended pattern is to perform a locked export into a customer-owned bucket (we can push into your bucket with pre-configured write permissions) and then you enable object-lock there. That preserves the chain under your control.

3) Deletion attestation: attached is a short template we use for attestations — includes manifest id, deletion request id, deletion completed timestamp, and list of object hashes. We can sign the attestation with our platform key.

Next steps: I'll book the 30-minute walkthrough for Tue 2027-09-07 09:30 PT and share calendar invite + dial-in. I'll include a short checklist for validation steps during the call.

—Karthik
Director, Security & Compliance Integrations
